title: Base change of the normalized negative-twist evaluation recipe
statement: Let A be a commutative ring killed by N>0 and t a normalized OrdinaryFiniteTwistTransport. For a commutative square g:Xprime->X, qprime:Xprime->Yprime, q:X->Y, f:Yprime->Y, with N invertible on all four schemes, suppose c:A_X->A_X(1)[2] and cprime:A_Xprime->A_Xprime(1)[2] commute with g-pullback under the prescribed positive comparison of t. Form z:q^* A_Y(-1)[-2]->A_X by inverse tensor right unit, tensor c, the canonical negative-twist pullback comparison for q, and p1DecompositionEvaluation; define zprime in the same way for qprime and cprime. Then the derived square comparison followed by g^*(z) and constant pullback equals qprime^* of the negative-twist comparison for f followed by zprime. All objects, shifts and comparisons are those of def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-decomposition-maps. This is an equation before adjunction, with no Cartesian, finiteness or properness assumption.

source.place: Definition of h by inverse tensor right unit, Chern class, and evaluation; the base-change argument uses naturality of this right unit.

proof.text: Composition of the normalized signed sheaf transport gives the commuting square for any signed exponent. Lift this square through the degree-zero embeddings by leftDerivedUpperStar_map_singleFunctor_comp. Then apply the proved shift-composition identity shifted_square to obtain signed_square for every signed shift.

Apply inverse image to the full evaluation recipe. Naturality of its tensor comparison in both variables, the evaluation and right-unit equations of finiteTwistDerivedEvaluation_pullback, and the assumed Chern-map equation identify it with the new-base recipe on the pulled-back source; this is the abstract pairing_pullback calculation.

Naturality of the prescribed inverse tensor right unit moves both precompositions through their recipes. The negative-twist case of signed_square identifies the resulting maps into the negative twist. The abstract recipe_pasting_point calculation proves the stated equality. These categorical identities also cover zero coefficients, N=1, empty schemes and nonreduced schemes.

theorem ordinaryFiniteP1_evaluationRecipe_baseChange
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A]
    (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N) (hA : (N : A) = 0)
    (t : OrdinaryFiniteTwistTransport A N hA)
    {X X' Y Y' : Scheme.{u}} {q : X ⟶ Y} {q' : X' ⟶ Y'}
    {g : X' ⟶ X} {f : Y' ⟶ Y} (sq : CommSq g q' q f)
    (hY : IsUnit (N : Γ(Y, ⊤))) (hY' : IsUnit (N : Γ(Y', ⊤)))
    (hX : IsUnit (N : Γ(X, ⊤))) (hX' : IsUnit (N : Γ(X', ⊤)))
    (c : ordinaryFiniteUnit A X ⟶ (ordinaryFiniteLine A N hA X)⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧)
    (c' : ordinaryFiniteUnit A X' ⟶ (ordinaryFiniteLine A N hA X')⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧)
    (hc : (ordinaryFinitePullback A g).map c ≫
        (ordinaryFiniteShiftedLinePullback A N hA t g hX).hom =
      (ordinaryFiniteUnitPullback A g).hom ≫ c') :
    let K := p1DecompositionTwist A N hA Y (-1) (-2)
    let K' := p1DecompositionTwist A N hA Y' (-1) (-2)
    let z := (derivedTensorSingleUnitIso ((ordinaryFinitePullback A q).obj K)).inv ≫
      ((ordinaryFiniteTensor A X).obj ((ordinaryFinitePullback A q).obj K)).map c ≫
      ((ordinaryFiniteTensor A X).map
        (p1DecompositionTwistPullback A N hN hA q hY (-1) (-2)).hom).app _ ≫
      p1DecompositionEvaluation A N hN hA X hX
    let z' := (derivedTensorSingleUnitIso ((ordinaryFinitePullback A q').obj K')).inv ≫
      ((ordinaryFiniteTensor A X').obj ((ordinaryFinitePullback A q').obj K')).map c' ≫
      ((ordinaryFiniteTensor A X').map
        (p1DecompositionTwistPullback A N hN hA q' hY' (-1) (-2)).hom).app _ ≫
      p1DecompositionEvaluation A N hN hA X' hX'
    (derivedSquareUpperStarIso (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) sq).hom.app K ≫
      (ordinaryFinitePullback A g).map z ≫ (ordinaryFiniteUnitPullback A g).hom =
    (ordinaryFinitePullback A q').map
      (p1DecompositionTwistPullback A N hN hA f hY (-1) (-2)).hom ≫ z'
